verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that Russujaponol A may interact with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3 through multiple indirect pathways. The drug is predicted to target GMP synthase [glutamine-hydrolyzing], which in turn is targeted by both Cochliomycin A, (rel)- and Aquilarabietic Acid H. These compounds, in turn, are predicted to have targets at Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. Additionally, Russujaponol A is predicted to target Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, which is itself targeted by Wikstroelide E, a compound that also targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The cumulative evidence indicates that Russujaponol A may influence the activity of the transporter family through a series of molecular interactions, potentially modulating the transport of organic anions across cellular membranes. The strength of the evidence is moderate, with varying scores across the different paths, suggesting that the relationship may be complex and context-dependent.
